record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: What is the precise order-one coefficient c′ in the axion-string version of the Weak Gravity Conjecture bound on string tension, T ≤ c′ f_a M_Pl, so that the resulting quantum-gravity constraints on low-energy effective field theory become quantitatively sharp?

evidence.quote: The Weak Gravity Conjecture places a bound on the tension of an axion string of the form T ≤ c′faMPl, but once again the precise value of the coefficient c′ remains an important open question [197] with applications to black hole physics [198, 199].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting and definitions. Consider a four-dimensional low-energy effective field theory containing a compact pseudoscalar (axion) field θ with periodicity θ ≃ θ + 2π and canonically normalized kinetic term (f_a^2/2)(∂θ)^2, where f_a > 0 is the axion decay constant. The theory is coupled to Einstein gravity with reduced Planck mass M_Pl. An axion string is a codimension-two solitonic object around which the axion field θ winds by 2π. Such a string has a finite tension T (energy per unit length).

A version of the Weak Gravity Conjecture for axion strings asserts the existence of an axion string whose tension obeys an upper bound of the form
    T ≤ c' · f_a · M_Pl,
for some universal order-one positive constant c' that does not depend on the specific effective field theory under consideration but only on the conjecture's normalization.

Problem. Determine the precise value (or the sharp optimal value) of the dimensionless order-one coefficient c' appearing in the bound T ≤ c' f_a M_Pl, in such a way that the conjecture provides quantitatively sharp quantum-gravity constraints on the low-energy effective theory (including, in particular, applications to black hole physics involving axion strings).
artifact.status_search_result: The axion-string form of the Weak Gravity Conjecture, T ≤ c' f_a M_Pl, has been formulated and motivated (e.g., Rudelius–Reece and related work on axion strings and the WGC, 2021), but the precise universal value of the order-one coefficient c' has not been pinned down. Recent literature continues to treat the determination of this coefficient as an open question with implications for black hole physics and EFT cutoffs.

status_evidence.title: The Weak Gravity Conjecture and Axion Strings
status_evidence.snippet: Formulates an axion-string WGC of the form T ≲ f_a M_Pl with an undetermined order-one coefficient, motivated by anomaly inflow and tower considerations.
status_evidence.claim: The axion-string WGC bound is formulated, but the exact order-one coefficient is not fixed.

status_evidence.title: The Weak Gravity Conjecture and Axion Strings (talk, Rudelius)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the bound T ≤ c' f_a M_Pl on axion-string tension within WGC, leaving the precise coefficient c' open.
status_evidence.claim: Determining c' is treated as an open problem.
